summary: We developed "Project Wally_ss," an interactive and responsive web application that functions as a virtual space map. To address the challenge, our solution allows young space enthusiasts to intuitively navigate the solar system using a zoom slider—traveling from Earth's orbit to the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Along the journey, users discover 8 historical artifacts left by NASA, such as the Eagle Lander, the Opportunity Rover, and Voyager 1. By interacting with glowing markers, users unlock immersive panels detailing each spacecraft's purpose, current status, and unique fun facts. This project is important because it transforms static historical data into an engaging, visual learning experience. By making the exploration of legacy space equipment interactive, we bridge the gap between past space missions and the next generation, sparking curiosity and inspiring future scientists.
details:
What it does & How it works: Project Wally_ss is a responsive, single-page application built entirely with HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript. It features an interactive "zoom" slider that allows users to navigate through different scales of the solar system (Earth's Orbit, The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space). Using CSS transformations (scale and translate) and absolute positioning, the map dynamically shifts focus. When users click on glowing markers, a glassmorphism modal appears, displaying accurate historical data about NASA artifacts (e.g., Eagle Lander, Opportunity Rover).

Benefits & Impact: By gamifying the exploration of historical space hardware, the project transforms static archives into an immersive educational tool. The expected impact is to spark curiosity among young students, making complex space history accessible and visually engaging.

Tools Used: HTML5, CSS3 (Flexbox/Grid), Vanilla JavaScript. The project was version-controlled using Git and deployed via a GitLab CI/CD pipeline. Claude 3.5 Sonnet (an AI Large Language Model) was used exclusively to assist in generating the foundational front-end code structure based on our detailed design prompts and provided NASA data.
